title: Stacked guarded levels are not inlined into a 2^k tree
verdict: plan and run stay small at 40 levels
description: Forty stacked projections, each appending a reach and a guarded column that read the previous reach twice (so an optimizer that merges projections by substitution would build a tree of 2^40 copies), plan and run in well under a second of engine time and under 100 MB of extra memory. Optimized plan text by levels (5, 10, 20, 40): 1,626, 3,784, 10,856 and 40,496 characters (`EXPLAIN`); planning 5 ms to 34 ms; running 3 ms to 27 ms; process peak 75 MB to 81 MB. The text grows about quadratically, not exponentially: every level keeps the columns of the levels below it, and the plan lists them at each level (up to 80 columns). The result matches the reference at every level.
reference: No reference counterpart: the reference has no plan size. D50-d needs the plan of a chain of k guarded levels to cost time and memory linear in k.

evidence.note: `python -m sverify_dev.guarded_columns p2 --engine duckdb`: DuckDB 2.0.0 (Python), Linux x86_64 (homelab); the P1 cases also ran on macOS arm64 for DuckDB and Polars with the same result.

provenance.notes: Issue #1719 (D50-d). Probe rows: 3000, every third one the text `bad`, which a strict cast rejects.
